policies.name: The assistant may only recommend a used car whose manufacturer matches the user's most recent request and whose price does not exceed the most recent stated budget
policies.formula_str: forall m . forall p . recommend_a(m, p) -> exists b . ( ( !(exists m2 . exists b2 . ( request_u(m2, b2) & (!(m2 = m) | !(b2 = b)) )) S request_u(m, b) ) & !(b < p) )

messages.text: I'm after a used Acura, and I can go up to $26,000.

Good news — I've got two you can choose between, so you're not stuck with a single take-it-or-leave-it option: a 2019 Acura TLX saloon at $21,500, or a 2020 Acura RDX compact SUV at $24,900. Both sit nicely under your number.
I love being handed a genuine choice rather than one car. The TLX is the saloon and the RDX the small SUV, right? Which would you keep yourself?
You've got them spot on. Personally I'd take the RDX for the extra practicality, but if you mostly drive solo the TLX is the sweeter steer.
It's mostly just me and the motorway, so the TLX it is. Let's start with that one.
